title: Spell Formula 1: f-strings
lessonSummary: Great! With f-strings you build sentences from variables and even do maths inside them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the output below.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Aria"
level = 5
print(f"Hello {name}!")
print(f"You are Level {level}!")

# Calculating inside the braces
gold = 100
bonus = 25
print(f"Your gold: {gold + bonus}")

# Several variables in one sentence
hero = "Thorin"
hero_class = "Warrior"
weapon = "Axe"
print(f"{hero} the {hero_class} swings their {weapon}!")

validation.expected: Thorin the Warrior swings their Axe!

title: Spell Formula 2: type() and the Four Elements
lessonSummary: You now know the four elements – and type() lets you determine each of them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: type() reveals the nature of every value.
tasks.codeTemplate:
spell = "Fireball"
level = 12
damage = 23.5
magic_active = True

print(type(spell))
print(type(level))
print(type(damage))
print(type(magic_active))

tasks.instruction: Determine the element of the variable level and print its type with print() and type().
Determine the element of the variable damage and print its type.

title: Fire: Text (str) and len()
lessonSummary: Fire elements are text – and len() counts every character for you.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
Use len() to print how many characters the spell has (spaces count too).

title: Earth: Whole Numbers (int)
lessonSummary: Earth elements are whole numbers – solid, countable and perfect for calculating.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
Create the variables level = 7 and hit_points = 120 and print exactly this line with an f-string: Level: 7, HP: 120

title: Water: Decimal Numbers (float)
lessonSummary: Water elements flow: decimal numbers with a point – and calculating with them gives decimal numbers again.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
damage = 23.5
hit_chance = 87.25
print(f"Damage: {damage}, hit chance: {hit_chance}%")
print(f"Element: {type(damage)}")

tasks.instruction: Create hit_chance = 87.25 and print exactly: Hit chance: 87.25%
Calculate the cost (price times amount) and print exactly: Cost: 10.0

title: Air: Truth Values (bool)
lessonSummary: Air elements are switches: True or False – and comparisons hand them to you automatically.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
magic_active = True
poisoned = False
level = 8

print(f"Magic active: {magic_active}")
print(f"Poisoned: {poisoned}")
print(f"Level above 5: {level > 5}")
print(f"Element: {type(magic_active)}")

title: Fusing Elements
lessonSummary: You calculate with numbers, you glue texts together – but Fire and Earth need a conversion.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
gold_a = 150
gold_b = 75
print(f"Total gold: {gold_a + gold_b}")
print(f"Difference: {gold_a - gold_b}")
print(f"Double gold: {gold_a * 2}")

first_name = "Luna"
last_name = "Silvermoon"
print(first_name + " " + last_name)
print(first_name * 3)

tasks.instruction: Divide gold_a by 3 and print exactly: Divided: 50.0
Print the first name three times in a row (no spaces) using text repetition.

title: Conversion Spells: int(), float(), str(), bool()
lessonSummary: With int(), float(), str() and bool() you convert elements into one another.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
age_str = "25"
age_int = int(age_str)
print(f"Text: {age_str} ({type(age_str)})")
print(f"Number: {age_int} ({type(age_int)})")
print(int(3.9))
print(float("3.5"))
print(bool(0))

tasks.instruction: Convert the text into a whole number, add 5 and print the result.
Convert the text into a decimal number and double it. Print the result.
Join the text with the level using str() and print exactly: Level: 9

title: Spell Formula input(): Consulting the Oracle
lessonSummary: The oracle always answers with text – int() and float() turn its answers into numbers.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and type a name into the input box, for example Blitz.
tasks.codeTemplate:

print(f"Welcome, {name}!")
print(type(name))
